The Movement of the Mode Under Held Coordinates and Kinks

Source: R/outer_refresh.R
mode_solver.Rd

Builds the solve that gives the movement of the penalized mode under a perturbation \(c\): \(v = -N (N^\top (K + D_m) N)^{-1} N^\top c\), with \(N\) a basis of the directions that the held coordinates and the kinks leave free.

Usage

mode_solver(spec, design, coef, K, Kinv, Dm, npar, offs)

Arguments

spec

A StatmodSpec().

design

The design at the mode.

coef

The coefficients at the mode, a named list.

K

The mode's penalized information, as ctx_penalized() returns it with laplace = FALSE.

Kinv

Its inverse.

Dm

The block's own curvature from mode_curvature(), or NULL.

npar, offs

The coefficient counts and offsets per parameter.

Value

A list with solve, a function of \(c\) that returns \(v\) without the sign; J, the curvature used in the solve; Dm, the curvature in which the held rows and columns are set to zero; hold, the held positions; and Ak, the kink constraints.

Details

The held coordinates are those pinned in \(K\) other than at a boundary (a coefficient that the criterion estimates, a direction that the model does not identify, a coefficient that a kinked penalty holds at zero). The kinks are the break-points that sit on an observation at the mode (kink_constraints()): there the one-sided slopes have opposite signs, so a small perturbation leaves the break-point on the observation, as a lasso leaves a coefficient at zero. Where the break-point's position is a single coefficient, that coefficient does not move; where it is developed over a design, the mode moves along the hyperplane on which the break-point stays on the observation. The solve is the bordered system of the equality constrained problem, written in the basis of its null space. The criterion's own determinant is not affected: it keeps the side convention of the break-point term.

Where \(N^\top (K + D_m) N\) is not positive definite, the solve uses \(K\) in place of \(K + D_m\).

See also

statmod_marginal_grad(), statmod_marginal_hess(), null_basis()
